whatChangedAndWhy: Two of last week's twelve posts were unmeasurable and it was my calendar's fault: I told the 10-27 beat to mint `symbol-thread:the-snake:...` when strategy's own pillar table says the family is `heartbeat:symbol-thread`, so the pair shipped under a family that does not exist and the scorecard filed it as (unrecognized). Fixed structurally — every beat in the new calendar now writes the full campaign value to mint AND the literal utm_campaign value to paste, so the drafter reads a value instead of a rule. I also opened one strategy PR (#6535): strategy Rule 2 has published a 14-opener banned list since 2026-08-11 and called it hard-blocked, but social/strategy-params.json only ever carried `did you know`, so 13 of the 14 blocked nothing — and I added `okay`/`ok`, because 4 of the 22 items posted 10-20 to 11-01 opened on one while all 22 still cleared the 6-word reuse gate, which cannot see a shared first word. The week-of-10-26 calendar put that shape off the menu in prose and it shipped twice anyway. The launch:photo-viewer arc, deferred twice, is placed: day 0 on 11-09, +2 on 11-11, +4 on 11-13, with day +8 handed to the 11-09 run; the slack arithmetic that deferred it clears now that a reserve day counts as landing slack. The lessons ledger is unchanged and I computed that rather than eyeballing it: zero edit/reject rows this week or last, findCodifiableRules returns nothing (autoCodify is false), findRetirableRules returns nothing (L002 is 3 weeks quiet against an 8-week window). One dark day, 10-28, and it was not a planning rule this time: the 10-27 and 10-28 daily-draft runs both failed at `Decide routine outcome`, and a reserve day's beat is never drafted a day early, so its fallback was never written.

calendar.text: 11-02 Mon — Decode thread hero, thread:hidden-clues:behind-the-data. November's first of six thread windows; the angle is computed, not chosen (ANGLES[(3+0)%5]). The thread as a dataset: count something real off the live lens before writing a word.

11-03 Tue — November's Mood beat, mood:era-match, rotating off October's mood:result. It goes early in the month on purpose so a mechanical failure still leaves time to retry — and it is the format whose 10-03 attempt was approved and then killed unposted by the 48h clock, so this is its first real airing.

11-04 Wed — Blank Spaces timeline, the week's permanent minimum. Next unposted chapter after Back to December / Lautner (shipped 10-29), confirmed-only and verified against the Vault. Tagged utm_campaign=timeline, not `thread` — four timeline items were mistagged `thread` in the week to 11-01 and vanished into the unattributable bucket.

11-05 Thu — news reserve 1 of 3, and the first half of Marjorie's re-draft ask #6520: the Patient Zero chart run (three weeks at No. 1, now No. 5). She asked for it as an extra pair by 11-04; an extra pair is unshippable because the poster ships one item per platform per day, so it takes the nearest reserve instead — one day late, but it actually ships.

11-06 Fri — Clue Web thread hero, thread:easter-eggs:quiz-poll. One question whose answer is genuinely inside the lens; check it is in there before writing the question. Not the motif 10-27's snake post already explained.

11-07 Sat — news reserve 2 of 3, and the second half of ask #6520: Brad Paisley inducting her into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame. An award, which §1(e2) counts as a major moment, and an elder of the room she started in saying she belongs in it.

11-08 Sun — news reserve 3 of 3. Fallback is Nelly surprising Houston for 'Just a Dream' and the detail he revealed fifteen years later: he left with $50,000 in a McDonald's bag. The money is the hook, the surprise is the setup.

11-09 Mon — launch:photo-viewer DAY 0. The pinch-zoom viewer has been live since 2026-07-18 and has never been mentioned once; the arc was deferred twice and is placed now. Hard gate first: pinch-zoom a photo on a phone, and if it does not work, do not draft it — we never tease unshipped or broken work.

11-10 Tue — news reserve 1 of 2 for the week of 11-09. Fallback is Colin Jost and Michael Che nearly getting stuck on 'Wood' on Millionaire. Every one of the 22 items posted 10-20 to 11-01 was earnest; this one is allowed to be funny.

11-11 Wed — launch:photo-viewer DAY +2, the proof. Day 0 says the feature exists; +2 picks one photograph with a detail that genuinely rewards zooming and makes the post about that detail, not about the viewer.

11-12 Thu — Runway thread hero, thread:fashion:origin-story (window 11-11 to 11-15). Why the thread exists and what it lets you see that scrolling a tag page does not, grounded in one concrete look — and not the Oscar de la Renta look 10-30 already used.

11-13 Fri — launch:photo-viewer DAY +4, the invitation: name a specific photo and ask what people find when they get close. A real question, not engagement bait. Day +8 falls on 11-17 and belongs to the 11-09 run, which owes an answer on whether this arc completed — the last two closed short.
11-14 Sat — Blank Spaces timeline, the week of 11-09's minimum. Next unposted chapter after 11-04's, in a different hook shape, and not opening on a quoted song title (both halves of 10-29 did).

11-15 Sun — news reserve 2 of 2 for the week of 11-09. Fallback is Taylor telling a room at a Toy Story 5 screening about Abigail — the friendship 'Fifteen' is about. Note: that moment's own site media is a video and this pipeline cannot post video, so the beat uses its photo pick and links to the item page where the video lives.

needsFromMarjorie.ask: The Tree daily-draft workflow failed two runs in a row on 10-27 and 10-28 and cost a dark day — find out why and make it alert instead of failing silently
needsFromMarjorie.why: Both runs failed the `run / run-routine` job at the `Decide routine outcome` step (runs 40540524433 and 40732305282). 10-27's beat shipped anyway because the 10-26 run had drafted it a day ahead, but 10-28's news reserve had no such cover — a reserve day's beat is never drafted a day early — so nothing shipped on either platform that day and its named 1989 fallback was never written. Nothing surfaced this to me until I read the run history in today's weekly plan.

needsFromMarjorie.ask: Add a sibling-opener check to check-drafts.mjs: fail an IG/X pair whose two halves open on the same first three or four words
needsFromMarjorie.why: Second week running that a pair shipped sharing its opening clause — 10-24 both halves on the same date-stamp ('twenty years ago tomorrow'), 10-29 both halves on the same quoted song title ('back to december'). No gate we have can see it: Rule 3's 6-word match passes because words 3-6 differ, and crossPost.similarityThreshold compares whole bodies, where a shared opening clause scores low. I have restated the sibling rule on every beat in the new calendar, but prose direction is exactly what already failed twice, and check-drafts.mjs is outside my mutation rights.
